course_name_original: Introduction to Optimal and Model Predictive Control (M2063)
course_name_en: Introduction to Optimal and Model Predictive Control

learning_outcomes.text: Students learn the basic techniques of optimal and predictive control for linear systems.
Students learn about the linear quadratic state controller and the basics of dynamic programming.
Students learn the basic idea of model predictive control for linear systems with quadratic cost functionals.
Students learn how the problems that arise can be solved using numerical algorithms.
Students are able to design simple optimal state feedback for linear systems.
Students can formulate discrete-time optimal control problems and solve them using numerical methods.
Students can formulate and solve dynamic programming recursion for linear systems.
Students can formulate simple MPC controllers and implement numerical ones.
Students can make statements about the nominal stability of the designed control closed-loop.
The students can collaborate across boundaries of disciplines and in international teams.
The student can formulate questions and problems with respect to complex issues.
They can program selected techniques on their own in Matlab or Python.

assessment_methods.method: Written elaboration (project documentation in report form)

assessment_rules: A written elaboration (project documentation in report form) can contribute 20% as a bonus. The main examination is an oral exam lasting 30 minutes.
